data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:12 | [2024-06-28 13:59] derbymanager : - I'm tweaking school training to be faster, hopefully it'll be better in the next days. Main squad training is working well. - Mentors have been simplified, they now give a fixed boost (the number written next to them)  to all senior and youth players in their group. The number is not divided by the number of players anymore. Each 1 is equal to 0.05 facility stars (e.g. 10 = half a star). Maximum is 30 points in a group (1.5 stars). - Slowed down form change for players. Previously they could jump almost a full step in a single day (e.g. they could go from superb to fine in only 2 days). - Board satisfaction is calculated daily based on your league position. It moves slower if you are new to the team and/or it's the beginning of the season. The baseline is 75% (you are exactly at season expectation) and better or worse position affects the baseline. For example, your expectation is to be 6th but you are 12th for the first half of the season, satisfaction will move down every day in that period. Then you get 3 wins in a row and get to 6th, it will go up a bit towards 75% but it won't be enough to completely negate the first half of the season. But if you continue to win and end up 1st at the end, by that time satisfaction should go above 75% (even though you were below the expectation in the first half of the season, the second half matters more and will probably put you somewhere above 75% in the end).

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:36 | [2024-10-01 16:16] derbymanager : **Updates to training** The idea is that a few players that are just right for your team grow faster than the others, while majority grows slowly or stagnates. I wanted to avoid all young players predictably growing and the game turning into farming simulator... So how does it work? It's quite complex as I wanted potential, club fit, playtime, age, facilities, mentors, and, of course, random to have a meaningful impact. I also wanted to hide all of that from us so that we don't have to worry about it 🙂  So, there are two things to observe with training: - The first and the more important one is how well the player develops. Players with good club fit **or** potential will grow faster. Good growth might mean they have low potential but great club fit or vice versa. Club fit is randomly generated whenever a player changes team and can be modified between seasons (and rarely during season). Potential is predefined for every player. Of course, amount of playtime dictates growth too and without it the player simply won't grow (except in school).  - Icons on the training screen will tell you how well your facilities work for your players. Some players might find the intensity too low, others too high, and some might simply be too good for your club. Changing intensity (selecting different skill to train from technical and tactical and turning mentors on or off) can help you put focus on your best growing players. Your goal should be to make a setup as good as possible for your best-growing players, which might mean sacrificing others that don't train well and leaving them with yellow icons.  In simplest terms, to gain the most out of training, give the most playtime to players that have the highest growth and, as a secondary and less important objective, set icons to favour those players.

You need to wait until the end of contract for him to demand 20k.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:69 | [2025-04-19 19:57] derbymanager : **New training**  - Potential. Every player has predefined potential. - Training level (intensity) combined with that potential sets the maximum power this player can reach in the club. - Optimal power is somewhere below that maximum power. - The further away the player is from optimal power, the worse he trains. - Team tier reduces the penalty for difference between current and optimal power.  So, increasing the training level with better facilities or mentors means increasing the maximum power this player can achieve in your team and the optimal power at which he trains.  Example (with imaginary numbers, the math below isn't right, it's just an example):  Current power is 10 A: Maximum power with training intensity 100 is 14, optimal power is 11, distance from current power is 1 B: Maximum power with training intensity 50 is 10, optimal power is 8, distance from current power is 2  Bigger team tier means smaller penalty for the same difference. E.g. if we assume two teams for which the above numbers are the same: - Team with tier 10 would get penalty of 10% for player A and 20% for player B. - Team with tier 5 would get a penalty of 15% for player A and 30% for player B.  *This isn't much different than how it worked before, the formula is simplified and intensity has bigger influnece on the overall training.*

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:86 | [2025-07-02 16:25] derbymanager : -----  **Training**  The idea behind the old training was that bad facilities mean you can still train players but you have less versatility when it comes to what you can train, while good facilities remove that limitation. This has made a lot of people very angry and been widely regarded as a bad move. So I made a few adjustments, but the general premise is the same: players train best when they play in a team that is above their tier.  - Your team's tier and player's potential and club fit set the maximum level he can reach. - Then there are variables that affect player's chance for a skill pop:   - 1st variable: Three training facilities each affect their own set of skills and define at what skill level player trains best the best. For example, facilities at level 7 will have the highest chance when training players with skill 7. The chance slowly drops so even with facilities at 1 there is a chance to increase the skill to 20, although this chance is lower than with better facilities.   - 2nd variable: Players with 2-4 stars will usually train the best. For low tier teams the peak can be even at 5 stars, but normally it's lower. The exact "peak stars" depends on player's club fit.   - 3rd variable: Player's peak training happens somewhere between their age of 18 and 25.   - 4th variable: Sharpness works as before. Sharpness of 0 means no training, sharpness at 100% means the maximum you can get from the first 3 variables.   But that's not all!   - To align with the new skill/training system, mentors provide fewer mentor points but as you can see they're even more important now. - Which skills belong to which training category has been changed (and makes more sense now IMO). - And most importantly, the skill you focus on has a small fixed chance to grow at all times (assuming the player and skill can grow at all). That means it can grow even for players that don't play and oldies. Normal training modifiers are added on top on this fixed base.
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:92 | [2025-07-17 21:55] derbymanager : **Yet another training update**  - Mentors now always provide a training boost, you don't have to turn them on or off. They also benefit from their own boost. There are no penalties whatsoever to someone being a mentor. Also, remember that each mentor point can be converted into 1M for facilities when you retire a player. - They, however, provide a boost to a single area only (technique, decisions, movement). It's predefined which. - Training level (facilities + mentor) now sets how far can a player grow in that category. This is based on player's potential - that part works the same as before, it's just now split in 3 types of potential:   - Movement skills get a boost to potential while young and a penalty when old   - Decisions work the opposite, older players have higher potential there   - Technical skills depend on club fit more or less... - Players will become progressively unhappy as they get locked out of certain categories because your facilities are not adequate. For now the penalties are reduced but start buying mentors because I will introduce them at the end of the season. Or improve facilities. Or both.  Reminder that players now train even if they don't play. It's not much, increasing their sharpness is magnitudes better, but the bottom line isn't 0 anymore. The selected skill also gives a fixed boost no matter their sharpness.  *In the end, bigger numbers are simply better, there is no optimisation beyond that. But you need mentors (in lower leagues especially, but also in higher) to train youngsters.*
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:93 | [2025-07-26 07:14] derbymanager : **Announcement for s14**  Oldies right now get certain boosts in the match engine but those are not shown anywhere and most managers are unaware of them. A lot of people (probably the vast majority)  therefore expect the same results from a 3 star youngster and a 3 star oldie on the pitch and might get frustrated that their young squad underperforms. So for the next season I will change how match modifiers work (sharpness, form...) and will represent them with a single icon that should tell you what to expect from each player in a match (e.g. for each player you'll know that this player will likely get yellow or blue face if you play him or whatever). In addition, I'll improve and explicitly show the boost oldies get from experience to showcase that these players are worth to keep.  The general concept doesn't change much. Youngsters vary in their performance. They can play great one game and bad the next one, while oldies give consistently good output on the pitch. This is, more or less, how it works now but it isn't obvious. I'll emphasize that a bit more both visually and in the code.  TL;DR. You need oldies both for training and results.  ps. oldies are 30+ but age is just one part of it and experience and skills play their part of course. Youngsters improve in price and can bring you money, oldies lose value but improve others and can bring you results. You need a healthy mixture of both.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:95 | [2025-08-01 14:10] derbymanager : **Season 14 update**  - **Previously mentioned changes.** As announced. - **Winter break.** On 20th day of the season (This season Sunday 24.8.) there won't be any matches. Instead your players will recover conditions and injuries so you can push for more. - **Prices have been updated.** The reason is that they were basically growing exponentially, almost cubically, which worked fine for cheaper players but made top players have unreasonably different prices even though they were almost the same. To put it simply, a couple of skill points more in right places would bring 5M player to 7M, but at the top those same couple of points would make 25M player worth 35M. Buying that 35M player was a trap because he definitely wasn't almost 50% better than the 25M one... So I reduced the exponent to bring down the prices of top players. Previously the most expensive player was around 60M, now he's around 40M. Buying the best players shouldn't be so punishing anymore. I tried to keep prices similar to where they were before but that's impossible and, as always, there are those who gained value and those who lost value... - **Potential affects price.** Potential was previously a small percentage increase on player's value which didn't really make much difference, especially for cheap players. Now it's worth more in terms of price but only if it's high enough. So, the youngster with high potential could cost significantly more than a similar youngster that is near his peak. You are paying for what he could become. If he doesn't reach those heights you might even possibly (although unlikely) lose money on younger players...  I'm off to my vacation, lose my number 😅

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:11863 | [2024-11-25 20:03] yasen_gg : I've been busy all day, so could barely respond. But the point I wanted to make is that there are multiple factors that need to align for you to get anything out of the training:  - You need to have at least one player with good potential and at the right time of development for him to start gaining very fast - Even if you lack the player that will explode in development, you still need 3-5 players in that group (Def/Mid/Fwd)   - If you train just for one person, you are throwing efficiency away - You need to actively manage to switch skills - You need to have the right facilities to make sure the skill you can train can even be trained to max level - You also need to make sure your player does not peak along the way or start requiring better facilities  And even when you do all the things right and finally get a skill to 20 - trust me you will not see the difference between marking 20 and marking 15 defenders. Apart from FCs and GKs who's efficiency you can directly evaluate in goals scored/conceded - you'll only see progress with the improvement of your team as a whole.  TLDR - for me, training is neither too fast, nor OP - you just get to have great periods, especially if you focus on having a squad full of youngsters.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:18780 | [2025-10-20 08:17] derbymanager : Development, on the other hand, depends on potential. Every player has "current power" (a calculation of how good he is right now in terms of skills) and a potential power that says how far can he grow. Potential is adjusted by club fit and the competition where he plays (team tier). No player will become a world class player while playing in 4th division. He needs to go to 1st division to become world class (assuming he has potential to even reach that far). Club fit is in there to make sure that potential isn't revealed simply by looking when someone started to complain about training.  Still, in a d4 team, a player with best potential will usually be able to grow more than the one with low potential. From manager's point of view, without metagaming, you would see a player grow and reach highest price in your team and he would ask to leave. You could then decide whether you want to sell him for the money or to keep him for his skills...

So I want to move a bit away from just power/price winning matches. The match engine didn't really change with this update but some other modifiers are in play now. So there are those club-fit and role-fit parameters that affect how your player plays. The goal with this is for players to form teams, not just collections of data objects. You will have players that will be club legends because they play great (have great fit) and those that just won't cut it. Those that play will get training which will help keep bots competitive as their first team will have 3-5 stars and the rest will have fewer. Which is how things work in real life. There is a strong correlation between first team players and prices 🙂 Simply put, those that play get seen and gather interest... data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:15297 | [2025-06-29 17:07] derbymanager : I agree training (and everything) could be better explained for new owners but that's not my goal at this point, I'm mostly focused on making things work well enough first. The game goes through many changes until I find what works, sometimes small adjustments have a butterfly effect across the game, and changing wiki again and again isn't fun for me.  That being said, I don't know what's there to not understand about training.  You basically have 3.5 variables: - your facilities (F) - player potential (P) - club fit, age and some other variables like age (C) - sharpness, not a variable like the others because you have full control over it (S)  And the formula is something like: P * (F + C) All numbers being better gives you the higher final result.  Then sharpness sets the percentage of that number you get as a training chance. If sharpness is 0, the player isn't training. If it's at 100%, the player is training as good as he can considering those 3 variables.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:2713 | [2025-07-31 10:08] derbymanager : I realized I didn't answer almost any of your questions 😅   > Like what to do at the start - which players do I sell, which players are worth buying at the start? Try to have 15 players with 3-4 stars in your squad. Better to have a good average squad than few top players and the rest all shitty ones. > How does the yout school work, when to promote youths? For a season you can observe 4 players in youth school. After 3 weeks you'll see their potential and all skills. If you like them, you can hire them. If you don't, you can find a new player at any time. When they reach their training limit in the school there will be a message so you can promote them if you think they'll get some playtime in your squad.  > Are players who are reaching their peak at the club worth keeping or should I get rid of them? On the training screen you can see a yellow or red icon that the player is close to reaching their peak in your team. That means that they could still grow but would need a better team to do so. If you're about to get promoted it might be worth keeping them. Otherwise you might consider selling them and buying some that can grow or that won't be unhappy. Having a couple unhappy players is ok, having half of the team unhappy is problematic. There is no right or wrong way, assess your squad and decide. * > What is sharpness and how important is it? Sharpness is increased by playing games and it's pretty important but not so much to avoid playing a good player with low sharpness. It grows quickly and it's basically here to promote rotating your squad so that you'd have more than 11 players ready to play at all times. > How much do mentors really contribute to the training? Quite a lot. They boost your facilities. > If I got w low-division club am I stuck with it for a longer time and should prepare to build it or do I get offers from better teams relatively soon? You'll get offers from better teams when you go up into 3rd division and survive there.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:2733 | [2025-08-01 00:06] furysk : For tier 4 teams i'd say that a guide would be:  have 3-4 players that are Lower division completed products.  these guys will want to lead a young team more than an established player might.  Ideally, you can also find players that will be prominent in a few different formations.  For example, a strong lower division 23-26 year old that can play a defensive game will usually have a lot of use, as will a more complete central defender.  whereas a veteran fullback winger or wide forward might not get the same amount of utility overall.  Pick and choose a few guys that can grow into the mentor position at the minimum, do not sell mentors unless you have a surplus in that age group.  Be willing to lose their TL potential, you are paying for their benefit to your team by missing on a few million.  Understand what each role does in the formation in this game, some roles do things slightly different than perhaps your favorite manager would use them IRL.  the tactics test screen is a good spot to see what the impact of each role is.  Spend a little bit more on the right unpredictable youngsters that have skills where you want it.  In tier 4, those guys that are ideally 2.5 stars but occasionally 2 stars, have high potential, and have great or superb natural fitness are most ideal.  They may be slightly worse than the 3 stars in terms of counting ratings, but they'll be easier to keep happy on lower facilities/mentors which will offset some of that.  The stars are almost less important to me than the spots where the ratings are best right now, have a good chunk of 2.5 stars that are super happy, and the turnaround since they have taken over for unhappy 3.5 stars is night and day (2-4-8 W-D-L first 14, 11-2-2 last 15), although tactical decisions have helped too.  the added bonus with 2.5's is cheaper wages, which means more cash in bank for you 🙂  others can help more beyond 4 than i can, just throwing what i know for this level 🙂

In d4 you get 2M for winning the league, 4M in d3. Everything below that is proportionally lower.  So if you can buy a 2M player and you have two options: A.) 31yo that has skills at 12 B.) 21yo that has skills at 10  Let's say that with player A you'll finish 1st and with B you'll finish 4th. In reality I doubt 1 player can make such difference but let's assume the most extreme scenario. That's a difference of maybe 500k in d4, 1M in d3... Probably lower because the difference in money between 1st and 4th is bigger than between 11th and 14th.  Player A will lose some value in that season, so whatever you earn extra will be lower. Keep in mind that we already assumed huge impact of this single player on your final position. It's not unbelievable that any extra you earn is completely negated with this one old player.  There is also boost to your reputation and possibly higher earnings later on if you get promoted, but that only matters if with that old guy you get promotion and without him you don't, which probably isn't the case for most teams.  There's also passive training boost, but that makes that player lose even more value...  On the other hand if you go with player B, there is a chance that player will earn you those 500k or 1M simply from training. Even if he stagnates, he most likely won't lose value.  In addition, player B will be better next season while player A will be worse. If in first season player B got you +3 positions on the league table, in 2nd season it'll be +1 position, and third season  B player is better.  ---  Now do the same math with 5 players and the gap becomes bigger and bigger.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part5.txt:14677 | [2025-08-22 21:33] yasen_gg : My rough ideas are:  - Playing a game consumes condition in real time - Performance depends on condition during the game - Fitness affects condition loss during the game - Injury chance increases as condition goes lower - Players can get both knocks and injuries    - Knocks lower condition after the end of the game (but player can play)    - Injuries make the player unavailable for selection - Sharpness affects starting condition - Condition recovery depends on facilities    - Low level facilities (D4-D3) provide post-game recovery allowing you to play 1 game per day easily.    - Mid level facilities (D2-D1) allow you to play 2 games per day here and there    - Top level facilities (Elite+) allow you to play 2 games per day consistently   This way: - Teams will be able to play their best teams more regularly relative to their club level - Subs will be used to provide you with a choice of how to utilize players that can't handle 90 minutes, while allow for others to get game time. - Injuries and knocks will further ask the question of whether you want to play someone 30 minutes, or maybe rest completely.  Anyhow, I've not thought through all of this deeply, but it's mostly the direction I lean towards if someone were to ask me.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part6.txt:3137 | [2026-06-20 17:12] furysk : My thoughts on the current system, and in general what i think is good or bad about it:  Good - It has brought the average age of a developing player down from what was basically 17-18 on the transfer list to 16-17.  That extra 30 days of development average for the people to utilize is very important imo in getting more mileage out of developing them, assuming their development age is close to their true age.    Good - the options available to train for lower level teams has expanded significantly.  Teams are less likely to settle on a few players in their school because of the age gap between school and the earliest available TL'd player (which takes a player exitting school or a team buying a guy out of school and TL'ing him at the earliest availability) and because of this more of the 'right guys' have a potential chance to be recruited in.  Bad - For higher level teams, this system is not nearly as helpful.  In some aspects, this design is a good thing, but they become reliant on finding a spot for lets say on average a 1M-1.5M at best prospect in their lineup card that would otherwise have a 10-12m player, meaning the cost of acquisition to them also has to include the potential value of losses incurred due to the fielding of that player, not just the amount they spent to bring them in.  Bad - it's a heavier overall investment cost now to find veteran players on the open market, because we're now dealing with not only lower understanding of veterans skills than when i first started but we are also dealing with a larger range of true valuation on the veteran players.  Bad - This system is reliant on human players not getting attached to a larger percentage of the players they develop, so that they are actually training players for sale value rather than trying to take them from league 4/tier 4 to the top.  I personally see too much wasted wage budget on middle aged guys that have stopped development because they reached the tier max that teams should have sold.

Buildup getting added - Also share this sentiment to an extent, but mostly because I LOVED watching full games. Abstracting away the buildup has been controversial, but I don't think the game is worse off.   4. Transfer windows - I was a big advocate of adding them because I hated how a given percentage of the contract is always wasted due to renewals happening before expiry. However, given how dynamic the game is and how often things change - being able to transfer players in and out is essential. Example - Alin knowing he'll be relegating a couple of weeks in advance has been spending his time to prepare adequately for next season. This would have been impossible if we had the transfer windows. Another example is how you play the game - you've made so many changes at Munster - now imagine joining and waiting a whole month before being allowed to tinker with the squad. I think down the line, having this flexibility of instant impact via the market is key and it's overall a positive.  5. Contracts ending end of the season ties up with the previous point, so won't be repeating myself.  6. I actually agree here - I've even been advocating for more player filled divisions and even adding timespan to the game, e.g. - we all play 3 seasons and then the game starts all over again and this is how we accumulate score. I also said to Derby that the first season of the game where there was not a single bot team in D4 was amazing. Chaotic, but amazing. Then again - there's a charm in being able to fight off the odds and win D1 against bots that were created as unbeatable. No one has done it yet, but it makes the chase even more tempting. So yeah - I think this one has tradeoffs, but I think both approaches are equally interesting/rewarding.  7. On mentors - I also kind of agree here - I don't really like how they work, I want them to exist, but I also have doubts about how they're currently being implemented. That being said - I know why Derby does things this way and I agree it's the right direction. The execution is not perfect, but I'm sure over time we'll find a way to make them feel less unpredictable.  8. On player graphs visible by default - I think this is a byproduct of the game not providing enough data. Seeing the spider graph is too powerful and I agree it should be hidden behind a scout usage, but if we had more overall team data, I think this problem will be solved immediately.  9. Also kind of agree as you don't really have proper training facilities, because everyone maxes out 1 of the 3 just so they can get max possible intensity from one of the areas. Splitting mentors over all 4 is stupid as well as we keep limiting our personal training to "Technical" only. And let's face it - everyone maxes out Technical because Finishing and Handling are the most important skills in the game. So yes - having training unified was more intuitive and allowed more freedom.  Overall, I think you are bringing valid points - there are issues in the game, but the game itself relies on players like you providing feedback. You've been with us for a long time and know how the game works (and how it worked), so it will definitely be a loss if you decide to stop playing (which I hope you won't).
